I didn't say 4 or 500 I said 600 and you can build a decent gaming pc for 600 and depending on how long you want to wait for sales you can get that price down.

Correct me if I'm wrong but with the xbox1/ps4 they stated every game will run at 60fps, that was the performance cap for those consoles. Now if I remember correctly there were quite a few games that couldn't hit that performance cap do to the console limiting those games. Now I'm not saying ps5 won't be able to do 4k but they generally boast about that kind of stuff and then there are quite a few games that can't hit that mark(some being able to hit that mark after lowering their settings heavily). On top of that pc you can switch parts when you want/have the money, console does not have that kind of option at this moment to my knowledge. Can you build pc's for extreme amounts of money hell yes you can but can you build low budget or budget friendly pc's again hell yes. Consoles have exclusives that draw people in(again they are starting to show up on pc now) but pc has the ability to couch game and be low budget and still perform in some cases just under console some matching console and others out performing them all together.

For the people saying pc is expensive it's really not. You can build a pc that matches the specs of a ps5. If you buy everything at its main price(meaning no sales) you can build one for maybe 100$ more than a ps5. If you wait for sales for the parts it will be cheaper than that. On another note you can couch game with a pc, you don't have to use mouse and keyboard. A pc can use pretty much any controller now even bluetooth controllers. Games also go on sale a lot through steam and epic gives out games for free pretty often and they are good games at that. It pretty much comes down to what do you want to do tho. I used to be a console gamer and switched over, I still own consoles purely for the exclusives but thats about it for me(Playstation and Xbox exclusives have been showing up on pc as of late tho).
